speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your cough, specifically how long it has persisted and if you have noticed any blood in your sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your recent incarceration and these symptoms, I need to ask if you have had any close contact with others who have had a cough or tuberculosis while in prison. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray shows diffuse infiltrates, which, combined with your history of incarceration and systemic symptoms, strongly suggests active tuberculosis. I will now request sputum analysis to confirm the presence of acid-fast bacilli. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_Smear

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal sputum smear does not rule out tuberculosis, so I will proceed with a more sensitive test. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: The sputum culture has confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which definitively establishes the diagnosis. I will now initiate appropriate anti-tuberculosis therapy for you. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
